title: Rung 8 -- a parallel projection, declared in the glTF

criterion.says: our own generated fixture -- rung 2 of the ten scenes read through a parallel projection

acceptanceClass.because: A fronto-parallel planar placement owns three continuous freedoms -- two of aim and one of scale -- and every distinct silhouette line costs one condition, so 2 + k >= E is what decides whether the construction can be written at all (`board/`). The glTF is ours and so is the camera inside it, so the freedoms ARE ours -- and the subject still cannot spend them: a cube's silhouette is six lines against three freedoms, and under a parallel projection its slopes are set by the orientation alone. The exact arm I.26.14 provides for is a fronto-parallel rolled triangle carrying an orthographic camera, and it is not built.

camera.note: The framing rule of board:0083 applied to this subject's own bounds: direction azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 at r = 1.73205080756888 m, and yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. The roll is -arctan(1/2) = -26.5650511771 deg, derived rather than set: for an edge of irrational raster slope the perpendicular pixel-centre offsets equidistribute over +/-0.5 px, so the smallest margin over L boundary pixels is about 0.5/L and it SHRINKS as the subject grows -- measured between 2e-5 and 1.8e-3 px here, under the oracle's own 5e-3 px jitter. For a slope p/q in lowest terms the same distance is exactly 0.5/sqrt(p^2+q^2) at every pixel centre in the plane and does not depend on L at all, and tan(45deg+t) and tan(90deg+t) stay rational whenever tan t does, so a roll of rational tangent keeps a rational silhouette rational. The previous -22.5 deg maximised edge-to-AXIS angle, which is not the quantity the comparison turns on. The SIGN is the convention src/gltf/Subject.cpp states: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. This subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so what the change buys it is a different draw of the same lottery and not exactness -- a property of the subject, and the reason its class is general-position.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.note: An orthographic camera is a different matrix and not a large number substituted for one, so the file declares one and both sides build it: ours through Camera::Projection's orthographic arm, Blender's through an ORTHO camera whose ortho_scale its importer sets to 2*max(xmag, ymag).

light.note: A coverage rung compares a mask. The only illumination is Blender's factory world, which costs nothing to match and is left where it is.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: Emission, one colour per node, and the geometry is untouched (board:0087). A Diffuse BSDF under a uniform environment reduces to rho*L only while no surface can be seen from another; where one can, Cycles at one sample takes ONE cosine-weighted direction per pixel and the answer is rho*L or exactly 0 -- a Bernoulli draw whose mean is the visible sky fraction, which is an ambient-occlusion estimator wearing a placement's clothes. A ShaderNodeEmission at strength 1 gathers nothing, so the world as a light, the sun's disk, a light's radius and visibility all leave at once. ONE COLOUR PER NODE because flat emission over touching bodies fuses their silhouettes: a misplaced node would hide inside the union, which is a worse instrument than the noise this replaces.

default.note: The binary mask. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe at another seed, and the whole of the emission case's acceptance. A Monte-Carlo estimator's answer depends on its seed; an emitter has no estimator, so the two dumps must agree bit for bit and any difference NAMES the integral that survived.

notes: xmag is ymag times the frame's aspect ratio, and that is not decoration: the engine's parallel projection carries the vertical extent alone, so a file whose two magnifications disagree with the frame's shape is refused by name rather than rendered with one of them silently dropped. Blender's importer takes ortho_scale = 2*max(xmag, ymag) on the larger raster dimension, which is the same statement at 1280x720.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the sum over the subject's triangles of the magnitude of the projected signed area, over 1280*720 at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the generated vertices
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so. The runner recomputes it from the generated vertices and refuses a mismatch. Every triangle is counted by the magnitude of its signed area, so a closed body counts its far side too and this is an AREA, not a coverage.
